chapter_note: This chapter reads as a homiletic analogy (sun → Mani and the elect) embedded in a formulaic discourse frame. It is dominated by application voice (imperatives, first-person self-reference) and institutional terms (disciples, congregation, elect, charity). No systematic cosmos→cosmos correspondential mapping appears; the analogy is used to point to Mani and communal ethics rather than to expound an impersonal cosmological mechanism.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic/container opening (“Once again he speaks… to his disciples… midst of the congregation”). No teaching content; pure editorial framing.

Imperative prompt (“Note how…”) and a naturalistic sun analogy used as setup for exhortation; not a closed correspondential system (no degree-structure, no cosmos→cosmos mapping). Functions as sermonic illustration rather than substrate exposition.

Strong application/self-referential voice (“I am like…”, “I will gather…”) plus institutional identifiers (“my children, the righteous elect… in every country”). The sun-ray imagery is used to point to Mani’s person and the community, marking it as later compositional/application material rather than impersonal core cosmology.

Direct exhortation and ethics (“I say to you… let him love… mix with them in his charity… be saved”), explicitly community-oriented. Even where elevated language appears (“the great glorious one lives in all of them”), it is deployed to enforce communal behaviour, not to describe a cosmological architecture.
